57159.question_text: Which of the following persons invented the punch card machine?
57159.explanation: Dr. Herman Hollerith developed the punch card system for data processing in the late 19th century, which was widely used for the 1890 U.S. Census. 57430.subject: Data Processing
57430.question_text:
The diagram illustrates the relationship between two tables in a database.

 

What type of relationship exists between Tables I and II?
57430.explanation: A one-to-many relationship is the most common kind of relationship. In this kind of relationship, a row in table A can have many matching rows in table B. But a row in table B can have only one matching row in table A.  A one-to-many relationship is created if only one of the related columns is a primary key or has a unique constraint.

57438.subject: Data Processing
57438.question_text: One of the advantages of a parallel database is
57438.explanation: A parallel database is designed to operate across multiple processors or nodes simultaneously. Its key advantage is parallel query execution, which breaks large tasks—such as complex queries or data analysis—into smaller parts that run concurrently on multiple CPUs, disks, or servers. This approach significantly speeds up data processing, making it especially effective for large-scale and big data workloads.

57443.subject: Data Processing
57443.question_text: In a relational database management system, files are organized as relations and
57443.explanation: A tuple, also known as a record or row, is a basic unit of data in a relational database management system (DBMS). A tuple represents a single instance of a relation, or table, in the database. Each tuple contains a set of values, or attributes, that correspond to the columns, or fields, of the relation.
